description: Schema-simplified feature list intended to be mostly atomic structural detectors. Excludes PAINS alerts and a few explicitly composite/heuristic shortcuts (strong_*_present, bidentate_chelator_present, base_sensitive, acidic_proton_present). (Updated: added a small set of composite/umbrella tokens needed by reactant_types taxonomy.)

features.description: Any sulfonate group attached to sp2 site
Any sulfonate group attached to sp3 site
Any aryl C–LG including aryl sulfonates
tert-Butyl group (quaternary carbon with three methyl groups)
Free boronic acid (not ester); hygroscopic, air-sensitive
Boronic ester; more stable than free acid
Primary amine (NH2); not amide/sulfonamide; highest nucleophilicity
Tertiary amine (NR3); not amide/sulfonamide; potential base/ligand
Ammonia (NH3) or ammonium salt; used as nitrogen source in arylation reactions (Ullmann, Buchwald-Hartwig)
Silyl ether protecting group on oxygen (TMS, TBS, TIPS, etc.)
Aliphatic alcohol; less acidic than phenol
Primary alcohol (RCH2OH); good nucleophile, easily oxidized
Secondary alcohol (R2CHOH); moderate nucleophilicity, oxidizable to ketone
Tertiary alcohol (R3COH); poor nucleophile, prone to elimination
Nitro group; strong electron-withdrawing, potential reduction
Aryl nitro; activates SNAr, can be reduced
Spirocyclic center; 3D character, increased complexity (carbon atom in 2 rings)
Methyl ether; permanent protecting group, requires strong acids/Lewis acids to cleave
Benzyl ether (Bn); cleaved by hydrogenolysis (Pd/C, H2) or strong acids
para-Methoxybenzyl ether (PMB); oxidatively cleavable with DDQ or CAN
tert-Butyldiphenylsilyl ether (TBDPS); bulky silyl protecting group, fluoride-labile
tert-Butyldimethylsilyl ether (TBS/TBDMS); common silyl protecting group
Triisopropylsilyl ether (TIPS); very bulky, stable silyl group
Acetate ester (Ac); simple protecting group, base or acid hydrolysis
Benzoate ester (Bz); more stable than acetate, requires stronger conditions
Pivaloate ester (Piv); sterically hindered, enhances stability
Acetal; protects carbonyls, acid-labile, stable to bases
Ketal; protects ketones, acid-labile, stable to bases
Tosyl (Ts) protecting group on nitrogen; electron-withdrawing, reduces nucleophilicity
Nosyl (Ns/2-nitrobenzenesulfonyl) protecting group; cleaved with thiols
Trifluoroacetamide (TFA) protecting group; more acid-labile than regular amides
Allyloxycarbonyl (Alloc) protecting group; cleaved with Pd(0)
Phthalimide protecting group; Gabriel synthesis intermediate, cleaved with hydrazine
Oxime; protects carbonyls, can be hydrolyzed back to carbonyl
Hydrazone; protects carbonyls, useful in Wolff-Kishner reduction
Methyl ester; common protecting group for carboxylic acids, base hydrolysis
Ethyl ester; slightly more lipophilic than methyl ester
tert-Butyl ester; acid-labile, orthogonal to other ester protecting groups
Benzyl ester; cleaved by hydrogenolysis (Pd/C, H2)
Thiophene; aromatic 5-membered S-heterocycle, π-excessive, metabolically stable
Imidazole; 5-membered heterocycle with 2 nitrogens, basic, coordinating
Thiazole; 5-membered S,N-heterocycle, common in drugs, π-deficient
Triazole (1,2,3- or 1,2,4-); click chemistry product, metabolically stable
Tetrazole; acidic, carboxylic acid bioisostere, metabolically stable
Quinoline; fused benzene-pyridine system, basic, drug scaffold
Isoquinoline; fused benzene-pyridine isomer, basic, alkaloid scaffold
Benzofuran; fused benzene-furan system, drug scaffold
Benzothiophene; fused benzene-thiophene system, metabolically stable
Benzimidazole; fused benzene-imidazole, drug scaffold (proton pump inhibitors)
Purine; nucleobase scaffold (adenine, guanine), kinase inhibitor scaffold
Pyrimidine or related; nucleobase scaffold (cytosine, thymine, uracil)
Morpholine; saturated 6-membered O,N-heterocycle, common solubilizing group
Piperazine; saturated 6-membered diamine ring, common linker in drugs
Piperidine; saturated 6-membered N-heterocycle, basic, common scaffold
Pyrrolidine; saturated 5-membered N-heterocycle, basic, proline analog
Epoxide; strained 3-membered ring ether, electrophilic, ring-opening reactions
Aziridine; strained 3-membered ring amine, electrophilic, toxic
Diazo compound; carbene precursor, highly reactive, explosive potential
Azide; click chemistry handle, explosive, 1,3-dipole for cycloadditions
Peroxide (O-O bond); oxidizing agent, explosive potential, autoxidation product
Isocyanate; electrophilic, toxic, reacts with amines/alcohols
Sulfonyl chloride; highly reactive electrophile, moisture-sensitive
Acid anhydride; acylating agent, moisture-sensitive, reactive
α,β-Unsaturated carbonyl; Michael acceptor, electrophilic at β-position
α,β-Unsaturated ester; Michael acceptor, conjugate addition substrate
α-Halo carbonyl; electrophilic, alkylating agent, lachrymator potential
Cyclopropane ring; highly strained (27.6 kcal/mol), unique reactivity, bent bonds
Basic ionizable group (pKa ~ 7-11); affects solubility, permeability, distribution
Acidic ionizable group (pKa ~ 2-10); carboxylic acid, phenol, sulfonic acid, tetrazole
Quaternary ammonium; permanently charged, poor cell permeability
Aromatic ring present (simple boolean for convenience)
Aromatic heteroatom present (n/o/s); coarse heteroaromatic indicator
Fluorine atom; metabolic blocker, lipophilicity modulator, bioisostere
Trifluoromethyl group (CF3); lipophilic, metabolically stable, electron-withdrawing
Difluoromethyl group (CHF2); hydrogen bond donor mimic, pKa modulation
Sulfone; polar, metabolically stable, hydrogen bond acceptor
Sulfonamide; bioisostere for carboxylic acids, drug scaffold
Urea; hydrogen bond donor/acceptor, kinase inhibitor motif
Carbamate; ester-amide hybrid, prodrug strategy, protecting group
Spiro center; single atom shared by 2 rings, 3D complexity, exit vector diversity
Bridgehead nitrogen; conformationally restricted, reduced basicity
Quaternary carbon; all-carbon substituted, no hydrogens, synthetic challenge
Benzylic C-H; oxidation-prone (weak BDE), metabolic hotspot
Allylic C-H; oxidation-prone, radical abstraction site, weak BDE
Propargylic C-H; acidic, potential for metal-mediated transformations
α-Oxy C-H; oxidation-prone, acetal/hemiacetal formation potential
Aromatic ketone; photoactive (Norrish reactions), triplet sensitizer
Naphthoquinone; redox-active, Michael acceptor, ROS generator
Aryl boron; Suzuki coupling partner, cross-coupling nucleophile
Vinyl boron; Suzuki coupling partner for vinyl transfer
Alkyl boron; less reactive, requires activated conditions for cross-coupling
Aryl stannane; Stille coupling partner, transmetallation with Pd
Vinyl stannane; Stille coupling for vinyl transfer, stereochemistry preserved
Aryl silane; Hiyama coupling partner, requires fluoride activation
Vinyl silane; Hiyama coupling, Peterson olefination substrate
Copper organometallic; cuprate reagent, soft nucleophile
Sulfide (thioether); soft nucleophile, oxidizable to sulfoxide/sulfone
Sulfoxide; chiral, polar, Pummerer rearrangement substrate
Sulfonic acid; strong acid, very polar, water-soluble
Sulfinic acid; reducing agent, SO2 source, oxidizable
Disulfide (S-S bond); redox-active, cysteine bridge, reductive cleavage
Phosphate ester; biologically relevant, leaving group in SN2
Phosphonate; phosphate bioisostere, stable to hydrolysis
Phosphonium salt; Wittig reagent precursor, phase transfer catalyst
Count benzylic CH2 sites (potential oxidation/alkylation handles)
aryl boronic acid - aryl boron reagent
aryl boronate ester - aryl boron reagent
alkyl boronic acid - alkyl/alkenyl boron reagent
alkyl boronate ester - alkyl/alkenyl boron reagent
alkenyl boronate ester - alkyl/alkenyl boron reagent
alkenyl boronic acid - alkyl/alkenyl boron reagent
alkyl organometallic (Grignard, organozinc, etc.) - organometallic reagent
aryl organometallic (Grignard, organozinc, etc.) - organometallic reagent
aliphatic C–H donor - alkyl C-H donor
acidic aliphatic C–H donor (α to EWG) - alkyl C-H donor
aryl C–H donor - aryl C-H donor
heteroaryl C–H donor - aryl C-H donor
Alkyl leaving group (alkyl halide or alkyl sulfonate).
Aryl boron reagent (aryl-B; includes boronic acids/esters/trifluoroborates).
Alkyl or alkenyl boron reagent (sp3-B or vinyl-B).
Heteroaryl leaving group (heteroaryl halide or heteroaryl sulfonate).
Diene (contains two C=C; coarse detector, mainly conjugated diene).
Dienophile handle (alkene/alkyne or activated anhydride; broad detector).
Hydride reagent / metal hydride (borohydride/aluminum hydride/hydride salt proxy).
Activated carboxylic acid derivative (acyl chloride/anhydride/activated aryl ester/PFP ester).
Ylide or phosphonate (Wittig/HWE reagents; phosphorous-containing carbonyl olefination reagents).
Acyl electrophile (acyl chloride/anhydride/ester; broad electrophile class).
Borane reagent (BH3 or borane fragment; coarse).
